bull.b: Achieving 99.5% median two-qubit gate fidelity at 108 qubits supports the credibility of Rigetti’s superconducting architecture. This technical performance can strengthen customer and government adoption, while providing a foundation for larger systems and future error-correction efforts.

Substantial liquidity combined with no debt gives Rigetti financial flexibility to fund processor development, manufacturing infrastructure, and customer deployments. This reduces near-term balance-sheet pressure and allows the company to pursue its technology roadmap without relying immediately on significant borrowing.

Rapid nine-month revenue growth, supported by on-premises system sales and customer and government programs, indicates expanding commercial and institutional engagement. Continued adoption across these channels could improve scale and make the business less dependent on a single customer or delivery type.

bear.b: Rigetti’s revenue base remains very small relative to its cost structure, producing substantial operating and net losses. Until revenue scales materially or expenses become more efficient, weak earnings quality will constrain self-funded growth and keep shareholder returns under pressure.

Negative operating and free cash flow show that Rigetti is not yet self-funding its operations or investment program. Continued cash consumption increases dependence on its existing liquidity and future financing or funding sources, particularly while research and capital spending remain elevated.

The industry has not yet demonstrated a clear return on investment against classical computing for data-center managers, delaying broad customer adoption. This extends the period before Rigetti can achieve meaningful recurring demand, operating leverage, and sustainable commercial profitability.
